subject: physics

moments.title: Zwicky's missing mass
moments.body: Zwicky measures velocities of galaxies in the Coma cluster. They move so fast they should fly apart unless there is ~400x more mass than the visible stars provide. He calls it 'dunkle Materie' — dark matter. He is ignored for 40 years.
moments.takeaway: Dark matter is hypothesised in 1933. The community files it under 'eccentric Zwicky'.

moments.title: Vera Rubin's rotation curves
moments.who: Vera Rubin, Kent Ford, DTM Washington
moments.body: Rubin measures the rotation of dozens of spiral galaxies. The outer stars move just as fast as the inner ones — they should be slower if Newtonian gravity from visible mass were all. Most galactic mass must be dark.
moments.takeaway: Dark matter is decisively established. Rubin is never awarded the Nobel.

moments.title: First strong gravitational lens
moments.body: Twin quasars Q0957+561 turn out to be one quasar imaged twice by an intervening galaxy. The galaxy's mass — much more than its stars — bends light.
moments.takeaway: Gravitational lensing weighs galaxies — and confirms dark matter.

moments.title: Bullet Cluster
moments.body: X-ray and lensing observations of the Bullet Cluster show the visible gas and the mass have separated after a collision. Dark matter passes through; gas does not. The result is among the strongest evidence for dark matter as a particle.
moments.takeaway: Dark matter behaves like a collisionless particle, not modified gravity.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Dark matter makes up 27% of the universe and 84% of all matter. Direct detection (XENONnT, LZ, PandaX) has so far found nothing. Indirect searches (Fermi, IceCube) likewise.
now.open_questions: What is dark matter? WIMPs, axions, primordial black holes?

reflection: Rubin's contribution is monumental and uncontested. She was never awarded the Nobel. The asteroid 5726 Rubin is named for her. Is naming planets and prizes for women a substitute for, or supplement to, real equity?
